versions.name: Fast hasher, index sized to workload

stress.note: The bitmap costs a bit set or clear whenever a level fills or empties, on a workload that never had a scan problem: about -4%.
Footprint stress: the whole ladder is touched. Still 0.76x of narrow. The profile points at cache misses in Slab::unlink, but that has not been isolated.
v4 scanned long empty gaps between levels (worst case 15.3 µs). The bitmap cut the worst-case scan to 0.01 µs.

stress.shape: ~4-9k resting orders, ~1.2k tick range, clustered stream
stress.note: Same type mix as narrow, but runs of same-type commands. 1.31x narrow; about three quarters of that gap is branch prediction.

environments.name: Apple M5 MacBook Air
environments.caveat: No hard core pinning on Apple Silicon. The timer tick is about 42 ns.

environments.name: AWS EC2 c5.xlarge
environments.detail: ap-south-1, Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0-1014-aws, Xeon Platinum 8275CL @ 3.0 GHz, 4 vCPU (2 cores x 2 threads)
environments.caveat: Non-burstable VM, no isolated cores. Threads pinned to CPUs 0 and 1, which sit on different physical cores.

limits: All workloads are synthetic. The generated stream draws command types i.i.d., which is harsher on branch prediction than a real feed.
Prices must fit the configured ladder size (65,536 ticks by default).
Single instrument, single engine thread, no persistence or networking.
Pipeline latency uses batch 1, because a latency measurement cannot batch. The p99.9 and max tails are nearly identical pinned and unpinned, and their cause has not been isolated.
Numbers from different machines are never compared in one table.
